body:
Bitwise operations on enums result in `int`, like `SomeEnum | SomeEnum == int`. The reason is simple: when you use bitwise OR on two or more different elements of an enum (e.g. `1 | 2`), it is not a fact that the result (e.g. `3`) belongs to the enum.

Enum as a type hint is only suitable for exact values. The result of bitwise OR operation on elements of an enum `T` is a new type `BitField[T]`. The set of its valid values is a set of all possible flag combinations. For example, if we have `enum MyEnum {A = 1, B = 2, C = 4}`, then the type `BitField[MyEnum]` will have the following valid values: `0`; `1`, `2`, `4`; `1 | 2 = 3`, `1 | 4 = 5`, `2 | 4 = 6`; `1 | 2 | 4 = 7`.

The core supports `BitField<T>`, you may have seen it in the documentation as `BitField[T]`, but unfortunately GDScript does not support it at the moment. So you have to specify `int` for parameters that are bitmasks.
